title: 2.1 Scales, Standards, Units (Prefixes)
description: Scales, Standards, Units (Prefixes) concepts and applications. Hard level, 20 questions.

questions.question: A scale has ten spaces between marks labeled 3 and 4. What does each small mark represent?
A student reads a red line halfway between 3.3 and 3.4. What is the reading to two decimal places?
Two students obtain different masses for the same object using local units. What is the main problem?
options: The units have no agreed standard now
The object changed mass in this topic
The balance is digital in experiments
The students used the same unit still
questions.correctAnswer: The units have no agreed standard now

questions.question: Which requirement for a measurement standard is described in the textbook?
options: Different people in different places get the same result
Only experts may use it now for students in the textbook
It changes with the season in this topic in the textbook
It is based on one persons palm in class in the textbook
questions.correctAnswer: Different people in different places get the same result

questions.question: Why do traditional units such as footsteps create bias?
options: They depend on the person using them
They use metric prefixes in the unit
They are defined by law for students
They are measured in seconds as well
questions.correctAnswer: They depend on the person using them

questions.question: Which statement about scientific notation is accurate?
options: The exponent counts decimal digits only

questions.question: How many significant figures does 2000 have as written in the textbook?

Which operation set is permitted on an interval scale?
